sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: An omnichannel AI support platform designed to handle customer inquiries across messaging and web channels using a knowledge base and retrieval-augmented responses.
The engineering work is complete. The product did not launch commercially. Its patterns and lessons informed the Leen AI operating environment.

sections.title: Customer-support problem
paragraphs: Support teams needed consistent answers across channels without manually repeating the same information. Static FAQ pages and ad-hoc chatbots did not maintain context or retrieve from an organized knowledge base.
bullets: Inconsistent answers across Telegram and web touchpoints
Knowledge scattered across documents without reliable retrieval
Manual escalation when automated responses were insufficient

sections.title: What was built
paragraphs: A support engineering stack combining structured knowledge, retrieval-augmented generation, and channel adapters for customer-facing interaction.
bullets: Knowledge base with retrieval pipeline for grounded responses
Support workflow logic connecting intake, retrieval, and response
Architecture designed for extension into broader platform primitives

sections.title: My contribution
paragraphs: Technical leadership across architecture, AI integration, and channel delivery. Scope included retrieval design, integration boundaries, and engineering direction for the support stack.
Team members contributed to implementation. This case study does not claim solo delivery.

sections.title: Completion and evolution into Leen
paragraphs: Engineering reached completion without a commercial launch. The company and product direction evolved toward Leen — a broader AI operating environment rather than a standalone support tool.
This is documented as lineage and learning, not failure. The support patterns (retrieval, channels, workflow thinking) carry forward into the flagship platform.
